storm.summary_layperson: No storms anywhere nearby tonight — just a clear, cold evening with a frost advisory from 9 PM, and the Sound isn't changing anything here compared with surrounding towns.
storm.local_effect_blurb: No marine-layer buffer: the air is already 3°F colder than the 60°F Sound at 4 PM and the gap widens to about 10°F by 7 PM as the air chills after sunset.
storm.detail_html:
Regional picture: KOKX radar shows no echoes at all within range, and there is no instability in the atmosphere (0 J/kg CAPE). Upper-level winds are strong (about 47 kt of shear from the west), but with no instability that shear has nothing to work with — it can't organize storms that can't form. High pressure (about 1029 hPa) is firmly in control.

Local modifier: none in play. The cove's usual storm protection comes from a cool Sound sitting under warmer air, which builds a stable layer that chokes incoming cells. Tonight it's the reverse: the Sound is 60°F and the air is 57°F and falling to around 50°F by 7 PM, so the water is warmer than the air all evening. There is no protective layer — but there's also nothing for it to protect against.

Most likely outcome: dry, clear and cold for the cove and every surrounding town alike. The only active alert is a Frost Advisory from 9 PM tonight until 8 AM Sunday — a cold-night concern for plants and anything left outside, not a storm risk.

What would change the call: nothing on the horizon. It would take new radar echoes upstream to the west, which no model guidance shows this evening.

wind.regime_label: Light gradient wind — no sea breeze, fading to a light offshore drift after sunset

hourly.shift_note: near calm after sunset, flipping offshore

wind.tactics_blurb: Drifter conditions: the cove's light southerly dies around sunset and flips to a faint north-northeasterly that never gets above about 4 kt. Stay center, keep the boat moving, and sail toward any visible ripple rather than a side of the course.
wind.tactics_detail_html:
Regime: light gradient wind, no sea breeze in play. There's no sea breeze to build today — the air (57°F) is already cooler than the Sound (60°F), an air–water temperature difference of −3.4°F, and a sea breeze needs the land at least 5°F warmer than the water to run. Regionally the flow is a light northwesterly behind high pressure: the airport stations read 8–10 kt an hour ago, but the neighborhood weather stations along the shore are nearly calm (about 1 kt on average) and the forecast model has the wind at just 2–4 kt through the evening.

The cove is doing its own thing right now. Riverside YC reads S 8 kt gusting 10 at 4 PM while the surrounding region is northwesterly — a big split (direction agreement across stations only 63%). Two shore stations east and west of the cove also show weak SSW puffs, so this looks like a shallow local southerly eddy along the western Connecticut shore, not a real sea breeze. Without solar heating behind it, it should fade quickly as the sun sets at 5:51 PM.

After sunset: the land chills fast on a clear, frosty night (air forecast near 50°F by 7 PM against 60°F water), which sets up a faint offshore land breeze. The model swings the wind from WNW at 5 PM through near-calm to NNE about 4 kt by 7 PM. Expect a dead patch around 6 PM while the direction flips — that's the most likely time for a race to stall or be abandoned.

Where the pressure is: in light north-to-northeast flow off the land, the breeze is patchy and the shoreline trees and houses cast wind shadows. Best average pressure tends to be mid-cove away from either shore, so stay center and chase visible ripples rather than committing to a side.

Confidence is low after 7 PM. The model data stops at 7 PM, so the 8–10 PM rows extend the evening trend — a steady, faint northerly drift is the most likely outcome on a calm, clear high-pressure night, but expect stretches of near-calm. For racers: 2–5 kt the whole window is drifter territory — light-air sail trim, weight forward and to leeward, and patience.

data_caveats: Model wind forecast available only through 7 PM — 8–10 PM wind rows extrapolated from the evening trend (lower confidence)
Riverside YC reading southerly while the surrounding region is northwesterly — local eddy; early-window numbers anchored to the cove observation
Airport (METAR) observations are about an hour old
NWS forecast period covers this afternoon only, not the evening
